lesson.title: Example Embedded Lesson (High School)

props.name: Prompt
props.content:
###### 01 — Multiple choice

## Which particles are packed into an atom's **nucleus**?

choices.feedback: Electrons live in the electron cloud around the nucleus, not inside it.
Correct. Protons and neutrons (nucleons) make up nearly all of an atom's mass.
Neutrons, yes. Electrons, no: they orbit outside the nucleus.
The nucleus has no electrons at all. Think about what carries positive charge.

props.name: Prompt
props.content:
###### 02 — Select all that apply

## Which of these are **noble gases**?

They sit in group 18 and barely react with anything.

choices.feedback: Chlorine is a halogen (group 17) and very reactive.
Argon: group 18, and about 1% of the air you breathe.
Nitrogen is in group 15. It's unreactive as N₂ but it isn't a noble gas.

props.name: Prompt
props.content:
###### 03 — Fill in the blank

## Carbon's atomic number is 6. How many **protons** does every carbon atom have?

props.name: Carbon protons
props.correctFeedback: Yes. Atomic number = number of protons, so every carbon atom has 6.
props.incorrectFeedback: The atomic number tells you exactly how many protons an element has.

props.name: Prompt
props.content:
###### 04 — Put in order

## Rank these from **smallest to largest**

Drag the smallest to the top.

props.name: Size order
props.correctFeedback: Nailed it: electron → atom → molecule → cell.
props.incorrectFeedback: Not quite. Molecules are made of atoms, and cells are made of trillions of molecules.

props.name: Prompt
props.content:
###### 05 — Matching

## Match each element to its **symbol**

Some symbols come from Latin names, so don't trust your first guess.

props.name: Element symbols
props.correctFeedback: All matched. Latin names explain Na (natrium), Fe (ferrum) and K (kalium).
props.incorrectFeedback: Some are off. Hint: sodium's symbol comes from 'natrium'.

props.name: Prompt
props.content:
###### 06 — Classify

## **Metal** or **nonmetal**?

Pick one for each element.

props.name: Metal or nonmetal

rows.incorrectFeedback: Copper is a transition metal, which is why it's used in wiring.
Sulfur is a brittle yellow nonmetal.

props.overallCorrectFeedback: Clean sweep. Metals are on the left of the staircase line, nonmetals on the right.
props.overallIncorrectFeedback: A few are off. Metals conduct and are shiny; nonmetals tend to be brittle or gases.

props.name: Prompt
props.content:
###### 07 — Complete the passage

## Fill in the gaps about **isotopes**

props.name: Isotopes passage
props.passage: Isotopes of an element have the same number of [[1]] but a different number of [[2]]. That's why carbon-14 has a larger [[3]] than carbon-12.
props.correctFeedback: Exactly. Carbon-12 and carbon-14 are both carbon; they just weigh differently.
props.incorrectFeedback: Check again: isotopes keep the same proton count but change something else.
